name: Tennessee
overview: Tennessee collects unpaid property taxes through a delinquent tax lawsuit: after February 1 but before April 1, the county's delinquent tax attorney files suit in chancery or circuit court. The property is then sold at a court-ordered public sale run by the court clerk, usually the Clerk and Master, and the sale becomes final only when the Chancery Court confirms the Clerk and Master's report of sale. Once the order confirming the sale is entered, the owner and other interested persons may redeem: within one year in most cases, 180 days or 90 days when the taxes were delinquent for more than five or eight years, and 30 days for vacant or abandoned property. Redemption interest is 12% per annum.

counties.how_to_bid: Sales are held online only at ZeusAuction.com, run by SRI. Register online with a bank account; payment is by ACH or wire from that registered account, in one installment within 1 business day of the close of the auction ($15 fee for wires). counties.how_to_bid: In-person auction run by the Clerk and Master. Bidders must be current on their own Knox County property taxes. Pay in full at the sale, or pay a deposit of the minimum bid plus 30% of the winning bid and sign a promissory note for the balance within 10 days. Cash, certified funds, cashier's check, money order or ACH only; no personal or business checks or wires. The minimum bid covers all due and delinquent city and county taxes. The redemption period starts when the court confirms the sale and may run from 90 days to one year.

Property is sold subject to a one-year redemption period from the Order Confirming Sale, with 12% simple interest per annum.

counties.how_to_bid: Properties with taxes delinquent two or more years go to a Chancery Court-ordered public auction held in the Montgomery County Courts Center; the property goes to the highest cash bidder. Pay by cashier's check or cash, in full within 2 hours of the end of the sale. All sales are final, and Trustee's Office employees and their relatives may not bid. The owner, lien holder or heirs may redeem for one year from the decree confirming the sale.
